## Required Library
```r
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)
```

## Syntax

```r
if_else(condition, true, false)
```
::: {.desc-item}
`if_else()` is a vectorised if/else function.
For every value in `condition`, it returns the matching value from `true` or `false`.
:::

```r
df %>% mutate(new_col = if_else(condition, true_value, false_value))
```
::: {.desc-item}
`if_else()` works especially well inside `mutate()` when you want to create a new column based on a condition.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## When should you use `if_else()`?
Use `if_else()` when you need a row-by-row choice between two values.
It is a clean way to do conditional calculations inside `mutate()`.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why not use base `if` here?
Base `if` works on a single TRUE/FALSE value.
`if_else()` is vectorised, so it can make a choice for every row in a column.
:::

## Examples

<div class="example-section">
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Classify tablet weights as pass or fail</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

tablet_weights <- read_csv("data/tablet_weights.csv")

tablet_weights %>%
  # classifies each tablet as pass or fail if it is within 5 mg of the target weight of 500 mg
  mutate(within_spec = if_else(abs(weight_mg - 500) <= 5, "pass", "fail")) 
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Correct dilution only for specific samples</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
library(tidyverse)

dilution_factor <- 10

assay_results <- tibble(
  sample_id = c("S01", "S02", "S03", "S04", "S05"),
  measured_conc_ug_ml = c(12.4, 1.8, 11.9, 12.1, 2.0),
)

assay_results %>%
  mutate(
    # Correct the measured concentration for samples S02 and S05 only
    corrected_conc_ug_ml = if_else(
      sample_id %in% c("S02", "S05"),
      measured_conc_ug_ml * dilution_factor,
      measured_conc_ug_ml
    )
  )
```
</div>
</details>

</div>

## Argument Overview
<p class="arg-intro">Required arguments must be included when using a function while optional arguments can be included on demand.</p>

::: {.arg-section}
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>condition</code> <span class="arg-types">logical vector</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
A logical test that is evaluated row by row.

```r
abs(weight_mg - 500) <= 15
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>logical</code></p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>true</code> <span class="arg-types">vector</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Values returned when `condition` is `TRUE`.

```r
if_else(abs(weight_mg - 500) <= 15, "pass", "fail")
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> any vector type that matches the output type</p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>false</code> <span class="arg-types">vector</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Values returned when `condition` is `FALSE`.

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> any vector type that matches the output type</p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>missing</code> <span class="arg-types">vector</span> <span class="arg-badge optional">Optional</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Value used when `condition` is `NA`.
If omitted, missing values in the condition stay missing in the result.

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> any vector type that matches the output type · Default: <code>NULL</code></p>
</div>
</details>
:::
